messages:
maya: heads up — over the last 20m we’re seeing sustained PCIe tx/util ~92% on rack-r32 in us-west-2 and a correlated egress spike from tenant=deepviz. latency tails on small-gen requests up ~120ms.

samir: yikes. is this noisy neighbor or job w/ huge transfer? any kernel traces?

maya: looks like kv-cache churn + frequent small requests causing DMA thrash. i pulled `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` and saw frequent mem copies. also NIC tx drops on host.

eli: can you paste the recent o11y link? i want the per-tenant flow view.

maya: https://o11y.redwood/hosts/rack-r32/topflows?from=-30m -> filter tenant=deepviz

ops-bot: alert: host rack-r32 NIC tx drops > 100/s for 10m, pci satur>85% (ticket 67890 opened).

jia: deepviz is on a shared fractional-slice dedicated pool, right? they have high qps but low token sizes, so batching is low and cost per token is high.

oliver: can we soft-quarantine them into a temporary carveout? or increase their dedicated slice to avoid cross-tenant interference?

samir: options: 1) immediate soft-quarantine (egress-limited carveout) 2) apply per-tenant egress policer on top of NIC shaping 3) encourage customer to use batching/kv-cache hints + longer sequences.

pm-aaron: deepviz is a paying customer on tier-2; we should avoid breaking SLA. what’s expected latency improvement per option?

eli: rough: soft-quarantine -> tails improve ~30-40ms, policer -> 15-20ms but preserves capacity for other tenants, slice bump -> best but costs extra and provisioning delay ~30m.

maya: quick probe: i can apply a temporary policer (egress 200Mbps) to deepviz on rack-r32 for 10m to see impact. non-invasive.

samir: do it. add a short tag so routing & billing know this was a mitigation: `mitigation:policer/4999990000`

maya: applying now: `sudo tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 200mbit burst 32k latency 50ms` then map tenant flows to class.

(20s later)

maya: policer applied. watching metrics.

ops-bot: update: ticket 67890 annotated: policer applied to tenant=deepviz by maya at 4999990015.

eli: initial effect — NIC tx drops down 70%, PCIe tx down to ~65%, qps tail reduced by ~30ms. looks promising.

pm-aaron: if this buys time we should propose longer-term fix: either dedicated hot-shelf for latency-sensitive small-gen customers or an auto-detect that routes high-frequency tiny-req tenants into a specialized low-latency pool.

oliver: agree. long-term tradeoffs: dedicated hot-shelf increases cost ~+18% for that AZ but reduces incident noise. automated routing needs model-tagging + historical seq-dist profiles.

samir: follow-ups: 1) maya open runbook for policer mitigation (how/when) 2) infra to prototype hot-shelf cost calc (oliver + finance) 3) ml platform to export request-size histogram for tenant (jia) 4) SRE to add a noisy-tenant detector alert (eli).

maya: i’ll write the runbook and add snippet:

```
# quick policer apply
HOST=rack-r32
TENANT=deepviz
ssh $HOST "sudo tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 200mbit burst 32k latency 50ms && /usr/local/bin/tenant-map --tenant $TENANT --class constrained"
```

samir: toss the runbook link here when ready. also add cost tag so billing can retro-charge if we convert to dedicated.

pm-aaron: i'll mock cost options and share with oliver. aim for a proposal by EOD tomorrow.

jia: i'll surface per-tenant histograms and a candidate threshold for tiny-req frequency.

eli: i'll add a noisy-tenant SLI: sustained PCIe>80% AND per-tenant small-req-rate>200rps for 5m -> page.

oliver: thanks. good catch maya. :thumbsup:

maya: +1, will keep an eye for 30m then revert policer if stable.

ops-bot: ticket 67890 updated: mitigation in place, next review at 4999990120.
